## Import Path

Import path adalah **string unik** yang mengidentifikasi sebuah package. Go menggunakan import path berbasis URL untuk package eksternal.

```go
import (
	"fmt"                          // stdlib
	"net/http"                     // stdlib dengan subdirektori
	"github.com/user/repo/package" // package eksternal
	"myapp/internal/database"      // package lokal
)
```

## Import Alias

Gunakan alias untuk menghindari konflik nama atau mempersingkat nama package yang panjang:

```go
import (
	"fmt"

	// Alias karena konflik nama
	mypkg "github.com/user/fmt"     // alias untuk package yang namanya sama

	// Alias untuk mempersingkat
	yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"        // gunakan yaml.Unmarshal bukan v3.Unmarshal
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println("standard fmt")
	mypkg.DoSomething()

	data, _ := yaml.Marshal(map[string]int{"port": 8080})
	fmt.Println(string(data))
}
```

## Dot Import

Import dengan `.` membuat semua exported identifier tersedia tanpa prefix package. **Jarang digunakan** dan umumnya dihindari:

```go
import . "fmt"

func main() {
	Println("no fmt. prefix needed") // bukan fmt.Println
}
```

## Blank Import

Import dengan `_` mengeksekusi `init()` package tersebut **tanpa menggunakan** identifier apapun darinya:

```go
import (
	"database/sql"
	_ "github.com/lib/pq" // mendaftarkan postgres driver via init()
)

func main() {
	// postgres driver sudah terdaftar ke database/sql
	db, _ := sql.Open("postgres", "...") 
	_ = db
}
```

**Kapan blank import digunakan?**
- Driver registration (database, image format)
- Side-effect initialization
- Interface compliance checks

## Package Visibility Levels

```
myapp/
├── main.go           (package main)
├── api/              (package api — bisa diimport dari mana saja)
├── internal/         (package internal — HANYA bisa diimport dari myapp)
│   └── db/
└── pkg/              (package pkg — konvensi untuk sharable packages)
```

Directory `internal/` adalah fitur Go yang secara **otomatis** membatasi akses dari luar module.
content_en:
## Import Path

An import path is the **unique string** identifying a package. Go uses URL-based import paths for external packages.

```go
import (
	"fmt"                          // stdlib
	"net/http"                     // stdlib with subdirectory
	"github.com/user/repo/package" // external package
	"myapp/internal/database"      // local package
)
```

## Import Alias

Use an alias to avoid name conflicts or shorten long package names:

```go
import (
	"fmt"

	// Alias due to name conflict
	mypkg "github.com/user/fmt"     // alias for a package with the same name

	// Alias to shorten
	yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"        // use yaml.Unmarshal not v3.Unmarshal
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println("standard fmt")
	mypkg.DoSomething()

	data, _ := yaml.Marshal(map[string]int{"port": 8080})
	fmt.Println(string(data))
}
```

## Dot Import

A `.` import makes all exported identifiers available without a package prefix. **Rarely used** and generally avoided:

```go
import . "fmt"

func main() {
	Println("no fmt. prefix needed") // not fmt.Println
}
```

## Blank Import

Importing with `_` executes the package's `init()` **without using** any of its identifiers:

```go
import (
	"database/sql"
	_ "github.com/lib/pq" // registers postgres driver via init()
)

func main() {
	// postgres driver is now registered with database/sql
	db, _ := sql.Open("postgres", "...")
	_ = db
}
```

**When is blank import used?**
- Driver registration (database, image formats)
- Side-effect initialization
- Interface compliance checks

## Package Visibility Levels

```
myapp/
├── main.go           (package main)
├── api/              (package api — importable from anywhere)
├── internal/         (package internal — ONLY importable from myapp)
│   └── db/
└── pkg/              (package pkg — convention for shareable packages)
```

The `internal/` directory is a Go feature that **automatically** restricts access from outside the module.

quiz.question_id: Mengapa import alias seperti `yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"` berguna pada contoh?
quiz.question_en: Why is an import alias like `yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"` useful in the example?
options_id: Agar package bisa dipakai dengan nama yang lebih jelas daripada nama terakhir di path
Agar package menjadi blank import
Agar exported identifier tidak perlu prefix apa pun
Agar package hanya bisa di-import sekali
options_en: So the package can be used with a clearer name than the last path segment
So the package becomes a blank import
So exported identifiers no longer need a prefix
So the package can only be imported once

quiz.question_id: Sintaks mana yang benar untuk memberi alias `rng` pada `math/rand`?
quiz.question_en: Which syntax correctly gives the alias `rng` to `math/rand`?
options_id: `rng "math/rand"`
`"math/rand" as rng`
`import rng from "math/rand"`
`alias rng = math/rand`
options_en: `rng "math/rand"`
`"math/rand" as rng`
`import rng from "math/rand"`
`alias rng = math/rand`

quiz.question_id: Apa tradeoff utama dari dot import (`import . "fmt"`) menurut lesson?
quiz.question_en: What is the main tradeoff of a dot import (`import . "fmt"`) according to the lesson?
options_id: Membuat semua exported identifier tersedia tanpa prefix package, tetapi mengurangi kejelasan sehingga biasanya dihindari
Membuat package hanya bisa dipakai untuk testing
Menjalankan `init()` tanpa memakai identifier
Mengubah package menjadi internal-only
options_en: It makes exported identifiers available without a package prefix, but reduces clarity so it is usually avoided
It makes the package usable only for testing
It runs `init()` without using identifiers
It makes the package internal-only

quiz.question_id: Mengapa blank import cocok untuk `github.com/lib/pq` pada contoh `database/sql`?
quiz.question_en: Why is a blank import appropriate for `github.com/lib/pq` in the `database/sql` example?
options_id: Karena kita butuh identifier `pq.Open` langsung
Karena package itu mendaftarkan driver melalui `init()` sebagai side effect
Karena blank import lebih cepat daripada import biasa
Karena `database/sql` hanya menerima package yang diawali `_`
options_en: Because we need the `pq.Open` identifier directly
Because the package registers a driver via `init()` as a side effect
Because blank imports are faster than normal imports
Because `database/sql` only accepts packages imported with `_`

quiz.question_id: Apa yang TIDAK bisa dilakukan dengan blank import?
quiz.question_en: What can you NOT do with a blank import?
options_id: Menjalankan `init()` package
Memakai exported identifier package itu secara langsung dengan nama package
Mendaftarkan driver database sebagai side effect
Memicu inisialisasi package
options_en: Run the package's `init()`
Use that package's exported identifiers directly by package name
Register a database driver as a side effect
Trigger package initialization

quiz.question_id: Apa yang paling akurat tentang import path di Go menurut lesson?
quiz.question_en: What is most accurate about import paths in Go according to the lesson?
options_id: Import path adalah string unik yang mengidentifikasi package
Import path selalu harus berupa URL lengkap dengan https://
Import path ditentukan oleh nama file `.go`
Import path hanya berlaku untuk dependency eksternal
options_en: An import path is the unique string that identifies a package
An import path must always be a full URL with https://
An import path is determined by the `.go` filename
Import paths only apply to external dependencies

quiz.question_id: Jika sebuah project luar module mencoba mengimpor `myapp/internal/db`, apa yang terjadi menurut aturan `internal/`?
quiz.question_en: If an external project tries to import `myapp/internal/db`, what happens under the `internal/` rule?
options_id: Import valid selama path-nya benar
Import ditolak karena `internal/` membatasi akses dari luar parent yang diizinkan
Import valid hanya jika memakai alias
Import otomatis menjadi blank import
options_en: The import is valid as long as the path is correct
The import is rejected because `internal/` restricts access from outside the allowed parent scope
The import is valid only if an alias is used
The import automatically becomes a blank import

quiz.question_id: Mengapa alias juga berguna saat dua package memiliki nama yang bentrok, seperti contoh `fmt` dan `github.com/user/fmt`?
quiz.question_en: Why are aliases also useful when two packages have colliding names, like `fmt` and `github.com/user/fmt` in the example?
options_id: Karena alias mengizinkan kedua package dipakai tanpa ambiguitas di call site
Karena tanpa alias salah satu package otomatis menjadi unexported
Karena alias menonaktifkan compiler error
Karena package dengan nama sama tidak boleh di-import bersamaan dalam Go
options_en: Because an alias lets both packages be used without ambiguity at the call site
Because without an alias one package automatically becomes unexported
Because aliases disable compiler errors
Because packages with the same name may never be imported together in Go

quiz.question_id: Pada contoh dot import `import . "fmt"`, pemanggilan mana yang menjadi valid?
quiz.question_en: In the dot-import example `import . "fmt"`, which call becomes valid?
options_id: `fmt.Println("x")` saja
`Println("x")` tanpa prefix package
`_.Println("x")`
`fmt->Println("x")`
options_en: Only `fmt.Println("x")`
`Println("x")` without a package prefix
`_.Println("x")`
`fmt->Println("x")`

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling tepat tentang direktori `pkg/` pada diagram lesson?
quiz.question_en: Which statement is most accurate about the `pkg/` directory in the lesson diagram?
options_id: Itu konvensi untuk package yang dibagikan, bukan mekanisme pembatasan akses seperti `internal/`
Direktori `pkg/` membuat semua package di dalamnya menjadi private
Hanya package di `pkg/` yang boleh punya `init()`
Go mewajibkan semua library berada di `pkg/`
options_en: It is a convention for shareable packages, not an access restriction mechanism like `internal/`
The `pkg/` directory makes every package inside it private
Only packages in `pkg/` may define `init()`
Go requires all libraries to live under `pkg/`
